page: Amazon Web Services m8g.48xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by 64-bit ARMv9 architecture. The system provides 192 dedicated physical cores utilizing AWS Neoverse-V2 silicon clocked at 2.7 GHz, with one thread per core and no simultaneous multithreading. It is configured with 768 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio at 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes 50 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, operates without bundled local NVMe storage, and contains zero hardware GPU accelerators.

Synthetic and real-world benchmark metrics reflect massive parallel execution capabilities alongside high memory throughput. The instance achieves top-tier results in stress-ng multi-core compute tests (314,260.0) and multi-threaded decompression (1,391.35 GB/sec), contrasting with middle-tier single-core performance. Large-block memory bandwidth reaches 895.04 GB/sec for uncached reads and 426.41 GB/sec for writes. The platform delivers top-tier throughput in data operations, logging 356.88 million Redis SET operations per second and high static web serving bandwidth at 168.21 GB/sec. Large language model prompt processing scales reliably with model size, recording strong throughput on medium 7B architectures.

The hardware configuration represents high resource density for scale-out distributed systems. Without integrated local storage or specialized accelerators, the instance relies entirely on external network-attached volumes for persistent data. This architecture is best suited for compute-heavy parallel workloads, large-scale Redis in-memory caching tiers, enterprise database systems, continuous integration compilation pipelines, and high-concurrency web microservices.
description: Amazon Web Services m8g.48xlarge is a general-purpose Nitro-based instance powered by AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processors running at 2.7 GHz. The system provides 192 dedicated cores without multithreading, paired with 768 GB of memory to maintain a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM balance. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 50 Gbps, with zero onboard local storage and no GPU acceleration. Benchmark profiles indicate strong multi-threaded scaling, posting top-tier results in parallel CPU processing, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Clang compilation tasks. Memory bandwidth is notable, reaching 895.04 GB/sec on uncached read operations and driving top-tier database transaction metrics, including 356.88 million Redis SET operations per second. With single-thread metrics occupying the middle tier, the instance achieves high efficiency when driving massively distributed enterprise workloads, in-memory data stores, high-traffic web tiers, and parallel containerized environments.
